scenario: A world-orchestra youth programme selects finalists if they have either elite rhythm skill or elite pitch recognition. A 5% wildcard also admits applicants with neither trait. Observers think rhythm and pitch are negatively related among finalists.

data.description: Selection is based on either of two strengths plus a small wildcard.

question: Among finalists, compute (a) P(rhythm | pitch, finalist), and (b) P(rhythm | not pitch, finalist). Is the negative association real or a selection artifact?

ground_truth.explanation: The underlying traits are independent, but conditioning on finalist selection induces a spurious negative association.

naive_answer: Rhythm and pitch seem negatively related among finalists, so they must trade off.
naive_trap: Selection on either strength creates collider bias.
